clue.text: Unveiling trees, touch fruit with bent cane

indicators.note: something bent has been twisted out of its original shape, so the letters are pushed into a new order

blocks.note: firs are a kind of conifer tree
to tap is to touch lightly
a pear is a fruit
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unveils a garden sculpture among the trees, touching fruit with a bent walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces run straight on: FIRS, TAP, PEAR, then CANE rearranged as ANCE, giving FIRST APPEARANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unveiling is the moment something is shown to the public for the very first time, its debut.

clue.text: Formalised union with new arrangement in time and space

indicators.note: a new arrangement literally means the letters are set out afresh in a different order

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A marriage made official brings a fresh arrangement of the couple's shared life and home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formalised union' reads like a wedding, but its fifteen letters are exactly the fodder for the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics treats spacetime as three spatial axes plus one temporal axis, so anything existing across both has four dimensions.

clue.text: Tries again to run lines, endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: actors run their lines when they practise a play

explanation.surface: An actor keeps trying again to get through the script, going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E from REHEARSE. 'Tries' is meant in the courtroom sense, not the sense of attempting.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case a second time is trying it again, the legal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Dump booze outside of a town in Ireland

indicators.note: one thing sitting outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: a tip is a rubbish dump in British English
perry is an alcoholic drink made from pears
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pours drink away on the edge of an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a tip is a rubbish dump, and perry is cider made from pears rather than apples.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a real town in County Tipperary, famous from the wartime song about the long way there.

clue.text: Groups hiding in photography labs

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it, concealed within the run of letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Gangs lurking in the darkrooms where photos are developed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle photograPHY LAbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyla are major taxonomic divisions in biology, the rank just below kingdom that classifies animals.

clue.text: Fulfilment staff turned up: soldiers in casual shirts

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top
placing one item in another means it is surrounded

blocks.note: a cane is a walking staff
T-shirts are casual shirts, so two Ts
soldiers are the men of an army

explanation.surface: A warehouse fulfilment crew arrives, with soldiers among them dressed in casual shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fulfilment staff' reads as warehouse workers, but the definition stops at 'Fulfilment'. T-shirts shrink to T, and two of them hold the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Enactment is the carrying out or realising of a plan or law, which is fulfilment in the sense of bringing about.

clue.text: Dreaded one uprising of a Russian leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the tsar was the ruler of imperial Russia

explanation.surface: A feared figure leads a revolt against a Russian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreaded' suggests fear, but here it means wearing dreadlocks. 'Uprising' sounds like revolution, but it only turns A TSAR upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians traditionally wear their hair in dreadlocks, so a Rasta is literally a dreadlocked person.

clue.text: Poles welcoming musical girl, the likes of Mary Poppins

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: N and S, the north and south poles
Annie is the orphan girl who is title character of the stage musical

explanation.surface: People from Poland greet a girl from a musical, alongside characters like Mary Poppins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it means the compass poles N and S, which hold ANNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Poppins is the most famous fictional childminder, a nanny employed by the Banks family.

clue.text: Evil, strange, barbarous, monstrous Lake Constance?

indicators.note: something barbarous is savage and uncivilised, so the letters are treated roughly and wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter, then rearranged
Loch Ness in Scotland is the lake famous for its monster

explanation.surface: A lurid description of Lake Constance, the big lake on the German-Swiss border, as a place of evil and monsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Constance' looks like one place name, but it splits: the monstrous lake is Loch Ness, and 'Constance?' alone is the definition, the question mark flagging the old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is an archaic form of constancy, meaning steadfastness or permanence, which is the quality of lasting for ever.

clue.text: Jolly boyo, missing football club, depressed

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been left out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: jolly times are fun
boyo is Welsh slang for a lad or chap, and chappy is a pally form of chap
FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club

explanation.surface: A cheerful Welsh lad is down in the dumps because he has no football team.
explanation.walkthrough: FUN CHAPPY loses its F and its C, leaving UN HAPPY. 'Jolly' looks like the opposite of the definition, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed and unhappy are close synonyms for being low in mood and sad.

clue.text: A Beginner’s Introduction: Science 101 cancelled for non-attendance

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is kept
something cancelled is struck out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word
taken as written
101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: A course title: an easy introductory science module is scrapped because nobody turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Science 101' reads as a starter course, but 101 is CI in Roman numerals, taken out of SCIENCE to leave SENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence is the state of being away, the plain opposite of attendance or presence.

clue.text: Adorn orangutan with stethoscope?

blocks.note: a stethoscope marks a doctor, abbreviated Dr
an orangutan is a great ape

explanation.surface: Decorating an orangutan by hanging a stethoscope round its neck.
explanation.walkthrough: An ape wearing a stethoscope would be a doctor ape, Dr Ape; the question mark flags this playful picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape something is to hang cloth over it in folds, a way of decorating or covering it.

clue.text: Compound rates I calculate with select elements discounted, using life tables?

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters are blended into a new order
whatever is discounted is left out of the count, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material
the letters of the word select are the ones taken away

explanation.surface: A finance clerk works out compound interest, discounting some items and consulting mortality tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound rates' and 'discounted' sound like finance, but they are the anagram and deletion signals. Remove S, E, L, E, C, T from the fifteen letters and rearrange the nine left.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries price insurance and pensions from life tables, the mortality statistics predicting how long people live.

clue.text: Fail to deal with right-wing extremism with a bit of history

indicators.note: the right wing of a written word is its right-hand end, so only the closing letters are kept

blocks.note: the last four letters of the word
a and an are the same article
an age is a period of history

explanation.surface: A government fails to tackle far-right extremism, with a history lesson attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-wing extremism' reads as far-right politics; here it just takes the right-hand end of the word extremism.
explanation.definitionFit: To mismanage something is to handle it badly, which is failing to deal with it properly.

clue.text: Praise pet that’s barking … to get bite

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and mad letters are jumbled

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as material

explanation.surface: Praise a barking dog and it may bite you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog picture, but it is British slang for crazy and signals the rearrangement; 'bite' is a noun here, a small snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is a small amount of food, and an appetiser is a small dish served before a meal.

clue.text: Team leader requests you do them

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: The team captain asks you to carry out their requests.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose description rather than a synonym: the things you do are jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work that someone is set to carry out, so they are things that you do.

clue.text: In Yorkshire, the philosopher’s wedding attire

blocks.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens 'the' to t'
Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the Swiss-French philosopher

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire philosopher's wedding clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'on t' moor'; the 's of 'philosopher's' is read as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothing and linen a bride collects for her marriage.

clue.text: Chinese coolness coming back around very softly, very cool

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the letters read backwards
going around something means surrounding it

blocks.note: yin is the cool, dark principle in Chinese philosophy
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very softly

explanation.surface: Chinese calm returns quietly, and it is very cool.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chinese thought yin is the cool, passive force to yang's heat. Reversed it gives NIY, which wraps around pp, the musical marking for pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy is a British informal word for weather that is quite cold or chilly.

clue.text: 16 fish, about three took flight with some laughter

blocks.note: pi is about 3.14
to take flight is to run away
ha is one burst of laughter

explanation.surface: A cold fish and three others escape, laughing as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the answer to 16-across, NIPPY, so the definition reads 'nippy fish': one that nips or bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranhas are South American fish notorious for their sharp teeth and snapping bites, so they are nippy.

clue.text: Mix up root and rip up dried petals

indicators.note: to mix things up is to jumble them, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardening instructions: pull up plants by the roots and tear them apart to make dried petals.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening picture hides a plain rearrangement of ROOT and RIP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a scented mixture of dried flower petals and spices kept in a bowl.

clue.text: Roots of Riemann zeta: only minus evens and half + imaginary included – that’s where roots come from!

indicators.note: the root of a word is where it starts, so just initial letters are kept
whatever is included is put inside, surrounded by the rest

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the five words
the first letters of the two italicised words

explanation.surface: A statement of the Riemann hypothesis: the zeta function's only zeros are the negative even integers and points with real part one half.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, a famous unsolved maths problem; 'roots' in the wordplay means first letters instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhizome is an underground plant stem that sends out roots and shoots, so roots grow from it.

clue.text: Provokes ire with artist fabrication

indicators.note: a fabrication is something made up, so the letters are built into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forger's fake painting provokes anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provokes ire' looks like one phrase, but the definition is 'Provokes' alone and 'ire' joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to annoy or needle them, provoking them to anger.

clue.text: Tyrannosaurus raised upper leg

blocks.note: its first letter, as in the familiar short form T. rex
something raised is high

explanation.surface: A tyrannosaur lifts its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it simply means HIGH, after the T of T. rex.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the part of the human leg between the hip and the knee.

clue.text: Step-sister’s heart put out

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of sister
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A stepsister is upset and heartbroken, like one of Cinderella's ugly sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins 'Step' to 'sister' in the surface, but 'Step' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Policeman’s undercover operation

blocks.note: first meaning: the singer who fronted the band the Police
second meaning: a con set up by police to catch criminals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' suggests a cop, fitting the undercover picture, but it means a member of the rock band the Police; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sting was the band's singer and bassist, and a sting is also slang for a trap set by detectives.

clue.text: Silly people name their belly buttons, sometimes

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
an innie is a belly button that dips inward, so some people have these

explanation.surface: Foolish people give names to their navels now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' looks like a verb in the surface, but it is just N; 'innie' is informal for an inward navel, as opposed to an 'outie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninny is an old-fashioned word for a foolish or simple person.

clue.text: Controversially, Roman wine bar serves nail polish remover

indicators.note: contra plus versed suggests turned the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an enoteca is an Italian wine shop or bar

explanation.surface: A wine bar in Rome causes a stir by offering nail varnish remover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controversially' is read as contra-versed, turned the other way. Enoteca is the Italian word for a wine bar or shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is the solvent in most nail varnish removers, used to dissolve the lacquer.

clue.text: Chaps joined at the hip, later awkwardly embracing the cheerleaders

indicators.note: done awkwardly means done clumsily, so the letters are rearranged
to embrace is to hug, so one part wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written
rousers are people who stir up a crowd

explanation.surface: Two inseparable men later hug the cheerleading squad clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaps' looks like men, but chaps are the leather leg coverings cowboys wear, open at the seat; join them at the hip and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy chaps are separate leather leggings, so fastened together at the waist they become a full pair of leather trousers.
